summary.one_line: Home and cottage bakers chronically undercharge and know it; paid pricing spreadsheets sell at $8-$29 but almost all are cake-focused, so a bread and farmers-market pricing and profit workbook at about $15-$19 is an open, cheap-to-build position for Loaf Ledger.

go_hold.subject: Loaf Ledger paid product
go_hold.rationale: Clear, repeated pain (pricing from ingredients only, fear of losing customers, not knowing the hourly wage) and paid templates at $8-$29. The audience is low-revenue (median $2,000 sales in 2016), so price must stay low and the product must pay for itself on one market day.
go_hold.falsifying_test: If the workbook is live and gets 300+ sessions in 60 days with zero sales, hold Loaf Ledger and fold its traffic into an email list. Owner-adjustable rule.

key_findings.statement: A 775-producer survey found median cottage food sales of $2,000 and median profit of $500 (2016); producers average 15 hours a week, mostly without employees.
Cottage food producers are overwhelmingly female, more rural than average, have below-median household income, and most make baked goods; farmers' markets are the most common channel.
key_findings.notes: Exact percentages are in the report's figures, not captured.

key_findings.statement: Paid bakery pricing tools observed 2026-11-10: $7.79 (sale from $12.99) Etsy sheet, $19 Payhip workbook, $29 Notion system, $59.99 app, Stocksmith from $20/month.
CakeBoss is listed at $149 one-time plus $20/year, per an aggregator page last updated 2021-05-29 (stale).
key_findings.notes: Check the vendor page before relying on it.

key_findings.statement: Paid bakery templates are mostly cake, cookie and custom-order focused, but bread is no longer empty: a free sourdough pricer (Feb 2026), a $47 sourdough calculator and a community 'Price Your Loaf' tool now exist.
key_findings.notes: Revised 2026-11-11 (v1.0.3). The gap is narrower than v1.0.2 said: the differentiator must be the market-day loop (log, waste, profit per market, price ladder), not the hourly-wage readout alone.

key_findings.statement: Educators name the core mistakes as pricing from ingredients alone, copying competitors, pricing from anxiety and not knowing the hourly rate.
Free calculators are plentiful (Omni, Craftybase/Stocksmith, Homegrown, many small pages.dev sites).

A free, no-signup sourdough pricing calculator launched in February 2026; it breaks cost per loaf into ingredients, starter, labour by task, packaging and energy, and shows the effective hourly wage at a chosen price.
key_findings.notes: Described from the creator's forum post; the tool's site was not fetched (robots).

key_findings.statement: Bread-specific paid pricing tools are priced well above spreadsheets: $47 for a sourdough calculator on Stan, $20 for a Gumroad recipe pricing calculator; an Etsy home-baker calculator at $7.95 shows 0 sales.

premium_product_recommendation.name: Loaf Ledger Bread & Market Pricing Workbook
premium_product_recommendation.format: Google Sheets + Excel workbook, no macros, phone-friendly input tab, one-page quick start
must_include: Ingredient library in grams with cost per gram and automatic unit conversion
Recipe costing by baker's percentage and batch yield
Packaging, market fee and mileage costs
'What am I paying myself per hour' readout (now table stakes: a free sourdough pricer shows it)
Price ladder: wholesale, market and pre-order
Market-day log: loaves baked, sold, wasted, profit per market
Printable price list for the stall
Worked example: a sourdough country loaf
Lead with what free tools lack: the market-day loop (baked, sold, wasted, profit per market) and a wholesale/market/pre-order price ladder
must_not: Give legal advice on cottage food rules (link to state resources instead)
premium_product_recommendation.why_they_pay: It answers the question bakers already ask (am I paying myself anything?) and pays for itself if one market day's prices rise by about $1 a loaf.
premium_product_recommendation.falsifying_test: Zero sales from the first 300 sessions on the product page within 60 days of launch.

evidence.statement: Paid comparables at $7.79, $19 and $29 are verified; the bread/market angle is the gap.
The hourly-wage framing matches the language bakers use.
Free and paid bread pricing tools now cover cost-per-loaf and hourly wage; none observed covers the market-day loop.

unit_economics.statement: A $17 sale nets about $15.65 after the estimated 5% + $0.50 fee.
At about $15.65 net per $17 sale, $100 a month needs 7 sales and $400 a month needs 26 sales. This is arithmetic on the estimated fee, not a forecast.
